text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Monday's Pakistani newspapers:
DAWN

- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto and opposition leader Nawaz Sharif, in speeches to the National Assembly on Sunday night, exchanged proposals for setting up an accountability commission and initiating a dialogue between the two sides.
- The Pakistan government has urged sugar mills to release their stocks from their mills to obviate artificial shortage in the market.
- Talks between the government officials and presidents of Pakistan's three stock exchanges on the crisis of the stock markets will continue on Monday.
- Karachi city observed a partial strike on the call of opposition parties in protest against the alleged killing of a worker of ethnic Mohajir National Movement by police.
- Bandits killed two police sub-inspectors near the Punjab city of Sialkot.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The State (central) Bank is considering to restore credit lines to commercial banks providing export refinance.
- There is no risk of Pakistan defaulting in repayment of foreign debts, said special adviser to prime minister V.A. Jafarey.
- The Pakistanbi government is likely to restore mobile telephone services in Karachi by the end of this year.
FINANCIAL POST
- Federal Food and Agriculture Minister Yusuf Talpur has threatened to control sugar if its price remains above 18 rupees ($0.50) per kg.
THE NEWS

- Port Qasim Authority is going to reinvite the private sector for the third time to build a liquid cargo terminal for handling edible oil and molasses after getting a poor response in previous calls for tenders.
- The Central Board of Revenue has refused to grant any exemption on slaes tax on the import of construction machinery and equipment.
- The Central Board of Revenue has requested the Ministry of Finance to reduce the income tax collection target for fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) by eight billion rupees.
THE NATION
- The Sindh province government has stopped issuing government advertisements to those newspapers which are refusing to implement the new wage structure for their employees.
- The Sindh province government is likely to allow cellular telephone companies to resume their operations in the province on a limited scale.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
